name: Bulking

lead: Bulking is a planned phase of eating above maintenance calories while resistance training, to add muscle and body weight for a broader, fuller, more muscular physique. It is the counterpart of cutting, which later strips fat to show the muscle.

The surplus plus protein provides the energy and material for muscle growth under progressive training. Reference sources state that the link between positive energy balance and muscle growth is well established, while lifters debate how much fat comes with it and whether natural lifters need it.

paras: Bodybuilders traditionally bulk in the off-season and cut before contests. Clean bulks use a small surplus; dirty bulks use a large one. Most people bulk for months, tracking weight and training progressively.

Larger surpluses add more body fat and may require a longer cut. Dirty bulking is mentioned in reference material as possibly affecting cholesterol and insulin sensitivity over time, and steroid use alongside bulking carries separate serious risks.

angle.text: Lifters bulk to add muscle size and get a broader, more muscular physique before a later cut. Eating a calorie surplus alongside resistance training is a well-studied route to muscle gain; how much fat comes with it is the debated part.

lead: Bulking is a planned phase of eating above maintenance calories, combined with resistance training, to gain muscle and body weight. It is the counterpart of cutting, in which fat is lost.[1]

Bodybuilders traditionally bulk in the off-season and cut for contests; the length of the surplus determines how much fat accompanies muscle gain.[1] In looksmaxxing communities bulking is discussed for building a fuller, broader frame, and also debated for its effects on leanness and the face.[2][3]
Wikipedia states that the link between positive energy balance and muscle growth is well established, while noting uncertainty about how much muscle is retained through later cuts.[1]

paras: Bulking means maintaining a calorie surplus to support muscle growth; the size of the surplus depends on goals, and a larger surplus or longer bulk adds more fat alongside muscle.[1]

Clean bulking aims to add muscle with little fat, usually with tracked calories and macronutrients and a slower pace. Dirty bulking uses a large surplus, often from calorie-dense food, and adds weight quickly with more fat, usually needing a longer cut later.[1]

Grokipedia gives clean-bulk surpluses of roughly 250 to 500 kcal above maintenance and traces the practice to strongman culture, Eugen Sandow and the Weider brothers, though this source is AI-generated and not independently verified.[4]

No studies found. Related research on energy surplus and muscle mass exists in resistance-training literature, but none of the studies reviewed for this entry examined bulking as a looksmaxxing practice.

Wikipedia lists excess fat gain, a harder cut and, over time, possible effects on heart health and insulin sensitivity as risks of dirty bulking, and notes that anabolic steroid use, sometimes combined with bulking, carries serious risks.[1]

Users on looksmax.org describe bulking after a long cut as a relief, with extra calories allowing more food and less cardio.[2] Others argue that natural lifters do not need a surplus beyond the first year of training or when underweight, favoring small surpluses instead.[3]

lore.intro: Bulking is discussed on looksmax.org as a way to build size, and as a trade-off with leanness.[2][3]

claims.claim: A calorie surplus is the way to gain muscle.
Natural lifters do not need to bulk beyond early training.
A small surplus of about 250 calories gives minimal fat gain.
